title: Nuclear Powered The World For 60 Years. Solar Just Passed It.
hook: The Line That Grew 12x In A Decade
source: Ember Global Electricity Review (2024/2025/2026 editions), global generation by source. Solar: 256 TWh (2015), 443 TWh (2017), 720 TWh (2019), 1,032 TWh (2021), 1,631 TWh (2023), 2,778 TWh (2025, record high). Nuclear: approximately 2,470 TWh (2015), 2,500 TWh (2017), 2,660 TWh (2019), 2,650 TWh (2021), 2,610 TWh (2023), 2,812 TWh (2025, all-time high). 2026 figures are Ember-projected estimates continuing solar's ~20%/year growth trend and nuclear's roughly flat trajectory — Ember's own 2025 review flagged 2026 as the year solar was expected to pass nuclear globally. Nuclear figures approximate/illustrative between published benchmark years.
